title: Use a pair plot to show every pair of a few variables as small scatters.
rule: Use a pair plot, a reference form, for three to five variables: a grid of small scatter plots, one for each pair, with each variable’s histogram on the diagonal. Keep one scale down each column and across each row.
use_when: A specialist asks how a few measures relate to one another, pair by pair, before choosing which to chart.

use_instead.when: One pair the story turns on

text: Small scatters show each relationship’s shape, which a coefficient cannot, and the shared scales let the eye run along a row. Past five variables the cells grow too small to read.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: No kit form: draw a pair plot from small scatter-named panels with histogram panels on the diagonal.
sketch_alt: A three-by-three grid: small scatter plots of each pair of three variables off the diagonal, and a small histogram of each variable on it.
